correctness.rationale: The exact positive covariance series follows from a nonzero analytic gauge. Euler–Maclaurin with g(0)=0 and g'(0)=2 yields the uniform -1/(6 beta^2) term and O(beta^-4) remainder, including derivatives. Positive-definite kernel convergence yields proper Gaussian analytic-field convergence; a nondegenerate (value,derivative) pair and Rouche continuity yield convergence of zeros. Edelman–Kostlan gives the exact profile and derivative correction. Gamma-shape-two and log-concave Stirling saddle estimates give respectively 1/(2 pi t^2) and exp(t)/(4 pi). The radial count includes and cancels the gauge derivative. Forty-five finite numerical consistency checks passed; these do not replace the proof.

It determines an entire limiting analytic zero process, a mixing law, explicit sharp two-sided intensity regimes and a universal second-order finite-exponent correction; these are connected, motivated structural properties, not an arbitrary coefficient or finite table computation.
